findings.F1: The book loses because it is short into sharp rallies. On its worst 1 % of coin-days the book lost -7.57 % while the coin rose +10.40 %, and on its best 1 % it gained +7.26 % while the coin fell -9.88 %. Its trades lost on average after fees on every coin, from -1.03 % (ZEC, 501 trades) to -2.34 % (XRP, 501 trades).
findings.F2: The book's trades do worse the larger the 10-day fall they enter on, the reverse of the idea. Trades in the most negative entry-forecast quartile lost -2.39 % on average (727 trades, median -2.37 %), against -0.71 % in the least negative quartile (727 trades). This matches the step-5 slope t of -0.02 on 1085 grid bars.
findings.F3: In flat coins (net move ≤ half the 30-day range), the next-5-day excess return is not graded by depth below the middle or by the size of the 10-day fall.
findings.F4: A coin's one-day move scaled by its 20-day daily volatility predicts the next day's excess return, graded on the down side.
findings.F5: Other patterns did not survive averaging by date, so they are not findings.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its usual daily move over the past 20 days, the more that coin rises over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: After an outsized down day a coin is a short to close or a long to take for the next day, not a short to open.
ideas.name: Outsized down day rebounds
